rounds.response: It was flagged because it reads like medical advice: definitive claims ("completely fixed", "WILL fix"), a product/dose recommendation, and an instruction to skip doctors — all of which can be harmful if taken as general medical guidance. I recommend replacing the exact "WILL fix" language and "No need for doctors" with the disclaimer above. I’m marking this as "borderline—needs human review" but can help tighten the wording if you want.
